ViTrox Corp's 9M26 results was a beat, with yet another record quarterly earnings driven by robust AI-related demand and broad-based growth across its core businesses. We expect earnings to remain supported by a robust orderbook, favourable product mix, and progressive capacity expansion. At above peers' valuation, the slower growth potential - given the high base effect coupled with higher risk premium from the global AI outlook - leaves behind a balanced risk-reward profile.\n- Above expectations. 9M26 core earnings rose >2x to MYR253m, above our and consensus' estimates at 81% and 80%. This was driven by stronger revenue growth and margins expansion from improved operating leverage and a favourable product mix, alongside a lower effective tax rate. The stronger operating leverage lifted PBT margins to 26.5% (9M25: 20.9%). Meanwhile, the effective tax rate declined to 15.1% (9M25: 25.7%), benefiting from ViTrox Technologies' (VTSB) tax incentives, lifting earnings margins to 22.6% (9M25: 25.7%).\n- Sequential net profit growth continues. 3Q26 revenue rose 29.4% QoQ to MYR485.1m, driven by stronger shipment fulfilment across the automated board inspection (ABI) and machine vision system (MVS) segments, supported by sustained demand for AI infrastructure and networking equipment. The stronger topline, coupled with operating leverage and favourable product mix, lifted PBT by 36.8% QoQ to MYR137m, with PBT margin expanding 1.5ppts to 28.2%. Consequently, core profit increased 56.8% QoQ to MYR118m (2Q26: MYR75m), further supported by a lower effective tax rate of 13.7% (2Q26: 15.5%).\n- Positive outlook. We expect earnings momentum to remain robust into FY27, underpinned by sustained AI-related demand and a healthy order pipeline, with incoming orders continuing to outpace shipment capacity. Planned capacity additions should progressively unlock the order backlog from 4Q26 onwards, accelerating shipment conversion and easing the record high book-to-bill ratio. Campus 5.0 (completion targeted by FY28) should drive another step-up in capacity, while renewed pioneer tax incentives provide further earnings tailwinds from FY27 onwards, in our view.\n- Earnings and TP. We raise our FY26F-28F earnings by 14%, 8%, and 7% to reflect stronger-than-expected order conversions as shipment volumes ramp up. We expect a favourable product mix, operating leverage, and continued pioneer tax incentives to support earnings growth into FY27. We raise our TP to MYR11.60, pegged to an unchanged 50x (+1.5SD) FY27F P/E. At 46x FY27F P/E, ViTrox's valuation already factors in substantial earnings growth, leaving limited headroom for further re-rating given the slower growth and higher risk premium outlook. Key risks: A slowdown in AI/hyperscaler capex or a broader semiconduction down-cycle, component shortages and capex delays, and margins pressure from Chinese competition and FX. The opposite represents the upside risks.\n\nSource: RHB Research - 6 Nov 2026\n\n##### Discussions \n\n Be the first to like this. Revenue was up more than 110% year-on-year to RM485.1 million.\n\nLooking ahead, ViTrox expects a favourable business environment for the remainder of the financial year and into 2027, supported by robust growth in the semiconductor sector, continued investment in data centre infrastructure and rising demand for edge artificial intelligence (AI) devices.\n\nThe company — which makes machines used to automatically inspect and detect defects in semiconductor components and printed circuit board assemblies — said it is seeking to capture a slice of the increasing complexity of AI accelerators and high bandwidth memory.\n\nNet profit in the first nine months of the year also jumped to RM254.8 million from RM87 million a year earlier, supported by sustained capital expenditure deployment from strong AI infrastructure demand and electronics manufacturing customers.\n\nRevenue for the period also more than doubled to RM1.13 billion from RM552.7 million.\n\n“The group will continue to exercise prudent cost management and operational discipline to mitigate potential risks from foreign exchange volatility and geopolitical uncertainties,” ViTrox said.\n\nNo interim dividend was declared for the quarter under review, though the company had paid out 1.18 sen per share in July.\n\nShares of ViTrox ended Thursday at RM10.60, down 30 sen or 2.8%, giving the Penang-based company a market capitalisation of RM20 billion ahead of the results announcement. \n\nEdited By Jason Ng","highlights":["ViTrox posts best\n\n...\n\nFriday 06 Nov 2026\n\nKUALA LUMPUR (Nov 5): ViTrox Corporation Bhd (KL: VITROX) is upbeat after the semiconductor equipment maker posted its best quarter since listing in 2005, as higher volume drove down unit costs.\n\nNet profit for the three months ended Sept 30, 2026 (3QFY2026) was RM118.6 million, more than tripled from RM34.7 million a year earlier, according to an exchange filing. Revenue was up more than 110% year-on-year to RM485.1 million.\n\nLooking ahead, ViTrox expects a favourable business environment for the remainder of the financial year and into 2027, supported by robust growth in the semiconductor sector, continued investment in data centre infrastructure and rising demand for edge artificial intelligence (AI) devices.\n\nThe company — which makes machines used to automatically inspect and detect defects in semiconductor components and printed circuit board assemblies — said it is seeking to capture a slice of the increasing complexity of AI accelerators and high bandwidth memory.\n\nNet profit in the first nine months of the year also jumped to RM254.8 million from RM87 million a year earlier, supported by sustained capital expenditure deployment from strong AI infrastructure demand and electronics manufacturing customers.\n\nRevenue for the period also more than doubled to RM1.13 billion from RM552.7 million.\n\n“The group will continue to exercise prudent cost management and operational discipline to mitigate potential risks from foreign exchange volatility and geopolitical uncertainties,” ViTrox said.\n\nNo interim dividend was declared for the quarter under review, though the company had paid out 1.18 sen per share in July.\n\nShares of ViTrox ended Thursday at RM10.60, down 30 sen or 2.8%, giving the Penang-based company a market capitalisation of RM20 billion ahead of the results announcement."],"summary":"ViTrox Corporation Bhd (KL: VITROX) reported its strongest quarter since listing (2005) for 3QFY2026, driven by higher volumes and lower unit costs. The new TP is based on an unchanged 48x FY27E P/E, the stock’s 5-year forward mean. ViTrox is also retained as the broker’s large cap semiconductor top pick.\n\n- Action: BUY — Target Price MYR12.80 (previously MYR10.50); upside of about 20%.\n- Earnings upgrades: FY26E–FY28E core net profit forecasts raised by 32–51% to MYR373m, MYR505m and MYR616m respectively, driven by stronger order deliveries, a favourable tax rate (about 6% effective tax rate in FY27E) and incoming capacity additions.\n- Above consensus: Revised forecasts are 19–37% higher than consensus net profit of MYR323m (FY26E), MYR409m (FY27E) and MYR433m (FY28E).\n- Key investment idea — demand multi-wave: Current demand is led by US hyperscalers, AI servers and chips to OSAT and EMS players. Maybank IBG expects the next wave from China as HBM capability matures and AI data centre build-out accelerates, reinforced by humanoid robotics and AI inferencing demand.\n- Order book signal: The book-to-bill ratio stood at 1.5x in 2Q26 and is expected to stay comfortably above 1x as capacity unlocks. Management’s 7–17% QoQ revenue growth guidance across ABI and MVS is viewed as conservative.\n- Capacity expansion in full swing: Campus 2 and 3 are running at >90% utilisation. New warehouses are being built to free up floor space, China operations are targeted for mass production by 1H27, and a new 500k sq ft facility is on track for completion by 2028 to support the next growth leg.\n- Key risks: Rising costs, a stronger MYR against the USD, and intensifying competition from China.\n\nAbove is an excerpt from a report by Maybank IBG. No specific 2026 backlog data beyond the 1.5x book-to-bill noted for 2Q26.","image":"https://www.minichart.com.sg/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ViTrox-Corp.jpg"},{"id":"https://testbenchreport.com/articles/vitrox-draws-bullish-coverage-as-ai-inspection-build-out-accelerates-741a33a7","title":"ViTrox Draws Bullish Coverage as AI Inspection Build-Out Accelerates — Testbench Report","url":"https://testbenchreport.com/articles/vitrox-draws-bullish-coverage-as-ai-inspection-build-out-accelerates-741a33a7","publishedDate":"2026-10-10T02:29:56.000Z","author":"Grace Kim","text":"ViTrox Draws Bullish Coverage as AI Inspection Build-Out Accelerates — Testbench Report\n\n# ViTrox Draws Bullish Coverage as AI Inspection Build-Out Accelerates\n\nAnalysts covering ViTrox have turned more bullish, citing an AI-driven semiconductor upcycle per The Malaysian Reserve. The call ties ViTrox's AOI portfolio to advanced packaging lines.\n\nBy Grace Kim October 10, 2026 3 min read 583 words\n\n## Features\n\n- ■ Analysts covering ViTrox have turned more bullish, citing an AI-driven semiconductor upcycle (The Malaysian Reserve).\n- ■ ViTrox is a Penang-based AOI vendor covering 3D SPI, post-reflow AOI, AXI, and industrial machine vision systems.\n- ■ Advanced packaging nodes such as CoWoS and HBM stacks require inspection at sub-10 µm pitches, within ViTrox's product envelope.\n- ■ AOI sits one layer downstream of ATE platforms such as Teradyne UltraFlex and Advantest V93000, measuring geometric integrity rather than electrical behaviour.\n- ■ ViTrox's Malaysian incorporation places it in the onshore-supplier preference tier under current US export-control rules.\n\nDevice photo ViTrox rides AI-driven semiconductor upcycle, analysts turn more bullish - The Malaysian Reserve — AI-generated\n\nAnalysts covering Malaysian automated optical inspection (AOI) vendor ViTrox have grown more bullish on the stock, citing an AI-driven semiconductor upcycle as the catalyst, according to The Malaysian Reserve. The sentiment shift places the inspection equipment maker alongside the second-tier beneficiaries of the AI accelerator capacity build-out — the suppliers whose order books track back-end packaging lines rather than leading-edge fabs.\n\nViTrox matters to the instrumentation community because its product line sits at the intersection of machine vision and semiconductor back-end test. The Penang-based company designs and builds:\n\n- 3D solder paste inspection (SPI) systems\n- Post-reflow AOI benches for SMT lines\n- Wire-bond and die-bond inspection modules\n- 2D and 3D X-ray inspection (AXI) for BGA, QFN, and package-on-package stacks\n- Industrial machine vision controllers and embedded vision cameras\n\nEvery product family feeds pixel-level data into operator-attended review stations or library-driven automated defect classification (ADC). That conversion point — image to pass/fail at line speed — is what ties ViTrox's roadmap to AI semiconductor demand.\n\n## What does the AI upcycle actually mean for an AOI vendor?\n\nAI accelerator production pulls three independent demands into the back-end test chain. Advanced packaging lines such as CoWoS, InFO, and chip-on-wafer-on-substrate require inspection at pitches below 10 µm, where human review is no longer a closed loop. High-bandwidth memory stacks push line-side inspection cadence into parts-per-minute-per-head territory, the speed class where ViTrox's high-speed 3D AOI platforms compete. OSAT and IDM capex on greenfield packaging lines translates directly into SPI and AXI system orders, the back-end equipment book that has historically driven ViTrox's revenue mix.\n\n## How does AOI fit into the semiconductor test stack?\n\nAOI does not replace wafer-level parametric test or automated test equipment (ATE) — it sits one layer later in the process flow. Where an ATE platform such as the Teradyne UltraFlex or Advantest V93000 measures electrical behaviour against a stored test program, an AOI platform measures geometric and surface integrity against a golden-image template or convolutional reference. The distinction matters to a test engineer: an AOI dataset is image data and cannot flag a marginally slow gate. An ATE pattern cannot see a tombstoned capacitor. ViTrox sits only in the latter category, and its procurement argument to customers is reduced false-call rate and higher first-pass yield at the line, not correlation to bench-test results.\n\n## What will analysts be watching in the next two quarters?\n\nThe instrumentation signals worth tracking are: SPI placement-volume order book, AXI shipment mix between conventional BGA and 2.5-D/3-D advanced packages, and ADC library releases that bake in the new defect taxonomy from HBM and CoWoS customers. The qualitative turn in the published note does not yet cite a specific order intake figure.\n\n## Does the bullish call raise a compliance question?\n\nThe adoption question this sentiment shift raises is whether Malaysian vendors in the back-end inspection chain can hold the onshore-supplier preference tier that US fabs and OSATs extend to non-China inspection equipment under current US export-control guidance. ViTrox's Malaysian incorporation places it inside that tier, alongside names such as Cohu and Onto Innovation. That geographical status is part of why the bull case holds at all, and it is also the variable that would unwind fastest if US-China trade rules shifted before the end of the next capex cycle.\n\nvia Google News: Machine vision inspection (Source)","highlights":["# ViTrox Draws Bullish Coverage as AI Inspection Build-Out Accelerates\n\nAnalysts covering ViTrox have turned more bullish, citing an AI-driven semiconductor upcycle per The Malaysian Reserve. The call ties ViTrox's AOI portfolio to advanced packaging lines.\n\nBy Grace Kim October 10, 2026 3 min read 583 words\n\n## Features\n\n- ■ Analysts covering ViTrox have turned more bullish, citing an AI-driven semiconductor upcycle (The Malaysian Reserve).\n- ■ ViTrox is a Penang-based AOI vendor covering 3D SPI, post-reflow AOI, AXI, and industrial machine vision systems.\n- ■ Advanced packaging nodes such as CoWoS and HBM stacks require inspection at sub-10 µm pitches, within ViTrox's product envelope.\n- ■ AOI sits one layer downstream of ATE platforms such as Teradyne UltraFlex and Advantest V93000, measuring geometric integrity rather than electrical behaviour.\n- ■ ViTrox's Malaysian incorporation places it in the onshore-supplier preference tier under current US export-control rules.\n\n...\n\nAnalysts covering Malaysian automated optical inspection (AOI) vendor ViTrox have grown more bullish on the stock, citing an AI-driven semiconductor upcycle as the catalyst, according to The Malaysian Reserve. The sentiment shift places the inspection equipment maker alongside the second-tier beneficiaries of the AI accelerator capacity build-out — the suppliers whose order books track back-end packaging lines rather than leading-edge fabs.\n\nViTrox matters to the instrumentation community because its product line sits at the intersection of machine vision and semiconductor back-end test. The Penang-based company designs and builds:\n\n- 3D solder paste inspection (SPI) systems\n- Post-reflow AOI benches for SMT lines\n- Wire-bond and die-bond inspection modules\n- 2D and 3D X-ray inspection (AXI) for BGA, QFN, and package-on-package stacks\n- Industrial machine vision controllers and embedded vision cameras\n\nEvery product family feeds pixel-level data into operator-attended review stations or library-driven automated defect classification (ADC). That conversion point — image to pass/fail at line speed — is what ties ViTrox's roadmap to AI semiconductor demand.\n\n## What does the AI upcycle actually mean for an AOI vendor?\n\nAI accelerator production pulls three independent demands into the back-end test chain. Advanced packaging lines such as CoWoS, InFO, and chip-on-wafer-on-substrate require inspection at pitches below 10 µm, where human review is no longer a closed loop. High-bandwidth memory stacks push line-side inspection cadence into parts-per-minute-per-head territory, the speed class where ViTrox's high-speed 3D AOI platforms compete. OSAT and IDM capex on greenfield packaging lines translates directly into SPI and AXI system orders, the back-end equipment book that has historically driven ViTrox's revenue mix.\n\n## How does AOI fit into the semiconductor test stack?\n\nAOI does not replace wafer-level parametric test or automated test equipment (ATE) — it sits one layer later in the process flow. Where an ATE platform such as the Teradyne UltraFlex or Advantest V93000 measures electrical behaviour against a stored test program, an AOI platform measures geometric and surface integrity against a golden-image template or convolutional reference. The distinction matters to a test engineer: an AOI dataset is image data and cannot flag a marginally slow gate. An ATE pattern cannot see a tombstoned capacitor. ViTrox sits only in the latter category, and its procurement argument to customers is reduced false-call rate and higher first-pass yield at the line, not correlation to bench-test results.\n\n## What will analysts be watching in the next two quarters?\n\nThe instrumentation signals worth tracking are: SPI placement-volume order book, AXI shipment mix between conventional BGA and 2.5-D/3-D advanced packages, and ADC library releases that bake in the new defect taxonomy from HBM and CoWoS customers. The qualitative turn in the published note does not yet cite a specific order intake figure.\n\n## Does the bullish call raise a compliance question?\n\nThe adoption question this sentiment shift raises is whether Malaysian vendors in the back-end inspection chain can hold the onshore-supplier preference tier that US fabs and OSATs extend to non-China inspection equipment under current US export-control guidance. ViTrox's Malaysian incorporation places it inside that tier, alongside names such as Cohu and Onto Innovation. That geographical status is part of why the bull case holds at all, and it is also the variable that would unwind fastest if US-China trade rules shifted before the end of the next capex cycle."],"summary":"Summary:\n- Analysts have grown bullish on ViTrox (Penang-based AOI vendor), prompted by an AI-driven semiconductor upcycle that benefits back-end packaging lines rather than front-end fabs. These feed into line-side defect detection and AI-based classification, aligning with AI accelerator capacity expansion.\n- The AI upcycle is expected to drive orders in:\n  - Advanced packaging lines (CoWoS, InFO, chip-on-wafer-on-substrate) requiring sub-10 µm inspection pitches.\n  - High-volume AXI needs for memory stacks (HBM) and package-on-package configurations.\n  - OSAT/IDM capex on new packaging lines, translating to SPI/AXI system orders.\n- AOI sits downstream of ATE; it assesses geometric integrity rather than electrical performance.
